messages:
alex.m: hey team :wave: I'm hitting a weird ValueError when running the python SDK batch helper for embeddings + rerank. I call the paginator over a large dataset and then feed batched vectors to the reranker and get: ValueError: expected dim 768 but got 1024. snippet: ```py
# using redwood SDK v0.9.2
vecs = client.embeddings.create_batch(docs)
# later
reranker.score(query_vec, vecs)
``` any ideas?

megan: which model(s) are you using for the embeddings and the reranker? also which SDK version (py vs js)? :thinking_face:

alex.m: python SDK v0.9.2, model: open-embed-lite-768 for most items but a few older cached items were created with open-embed-large-1024. stack: `ValueError: expected second dimension 768 but got 1024` when concatenating batches.

ryan: sounds like a classic mixed-model cache issue — some items in your DB were embedded with 1024-dim model. reranker expects uniform dims. two quick fixes: 1) normalize to a target dim (re-embed or drop mismatches) 2) detect mismatch early and fail with a clear msg. We have emb_batch_utils that can split by dim before batching.

sophie: JS SDK quirk note: streaming embedding endpoints sometimes send partial events (like chunked vectors) and a naive concatenation can yield wrong shapes until the final "end" event. in py you might be buffering wrong if you assume each chunk is a full vector. make sure to wait for final object.

alex.m: re retries — I'm also seeing intermittent 429s while paginating. what's the recommended client config? I'm currently doing `retries=3, backoff=0.5` in a custom loop.

infra-bot: automatic note: API responses include `Retry-After` headers. recommended backoff: exponential with jitter. example config: `{retries: 5, backoff_factor: 2, jitter: true}`. also look for `x-rate-limit` headers for per-minute quotas.

megan: for caching and determinism, try grouping by model version before batching. it keeps batch shapes uniform and also improves cache hit rate. small helper: pad vs re-embed — padding vectors across dims is dangerous, prefer re-embedding to maintain quality.

alex.m: would love a small helper to validate dims pre-batch. I put together this quick func — thoughts? ```py
def validate_embed_batch(vecs, expected_dim):
    bad = [i for i,v in enumerate(vecs) if len(v) != expected_dim]
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"dimension mismatch at indices {bad}, expected {expected_dim}")
    return True
```

ryan: looks fine. consider using `model_registry.get_dim(model_name)` to infer expected_dim instead of hardcoding. also log the model version used per document when you ingest so you can backfill.

sophie: I'll open a tiny SDK PR to add a dimension-checking option to the python helper that raises a clearer error and suggests a remediation (re-embed / drop). can you @ me a repro or a minimal dataset?

alex.m: will paste a minimal repro gist in a sec. thanks! :thumbsup:

devx-bot: created issue #4521 (sdk-embeddings) from thread by alex.m and assigned to sophie. link: https://git.internal/redwood/issues/4521

alex.m: quick follow-up — after adding the validate step i still get occasional 429s when looping many pages. i'm going to stagger with random sleep(0.1-0.5) and rely on infra-bot advice. will report back.

sophie: PR opened: `fix/emb-dim-check-4521`, adds early validation and improved error message. tagging @alex.m for test.

alex.m: PR LGTM, tests pass locally. merging and cutting a 0.9.3 patch. i'll monitor for any more dim errors or streaming weirdness. thanks everyone!

ryan: thanks for driving this. a couple follow-ups to capture: (1) add telemetry event when embeddings with unexpected dim are encountered, (2) add a small CLI to scan cached DBs for mixed dims. happy to pair on 2.

alex.m: noted — i'll create tickets for both. closing loop for now, will re-open if 429s persist.
